description: Ninth held-out set: twenty-seven tasks, three per target skill, written after the eighth set was frozen and never tuned against. Each has an organic prompt, judge-only criteria, and a hidden acceptance check under holdout-v9-checks/ that the agent never sees.

claim.prompt: Rosa Ortiz has complained about her October bill from the laundrette. `npm run bills -- 2026-10` in agent-suites/fixtures/laundrette charges her £43.60, but her receipts only add up to £31.40. She had a couple of programmes restarted by the attendant that month, so I think the restarts are being charged as new washes. Can you fix it?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: bill() in src/billing.mjs matches cards with `entry.card.includes(card)`, so C1 (Rosa) is also charged for every upper-case C12 (Wen Li) programme and C2 (Ben) for C21's (Dara). The restart theory is checked and rejected with evidence: bill() already keeps only `start` lines, and charging Rosa's three restarts would add £10.50, not the £12.20 gap.

It finds the second fault the first one hides: the replacement dryer D2 logs cards in lower case (`c1`, `c12`), which neither the substring match nor a plain `===` bills, so every customer's D2 drying is missing. The fix matches whole cards case-insensitively (or normalises the log), rather than editing the log or the customer list.
A regression test covers a card that is a prefix of another (C1 and C12 or similar) and a lower-case card read, and the existing tests still pass.

`npm run bills -- 2026-10` is rerun and shows C1 £31.40 (9 programmes), C2 £17.10, C3 £14.10, C12 £23.20 and C21 £19.10. The reply says who was over- and under-billed and by how much (Rosa and Ben overcharged, Ivy, Wen and Dara undercharged for the dryer), and its claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: The booking sheet in agent-suites/fixtures/blood-drive is turning donors away. `npm run clinic -- 2026-11-03` says Priya Nair isn't due, but she last gave on 10 August, which is 84 days before the 2nd, so she should be fine on the 3rd. The clocks went back on 25 October and I reckon the gap is being worked out in hours somewhere and coming up a day short. Can you fix it before Tuesday's session?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: lastDonation() in src/eligibility.mjs takes every visit as a donation, so Priya's 14 September deferral (sent home for low iron, outcome `deferred`) becomes her last donation and she shows as due from 7 December. Tomas Weber (D02) is refused for the same reason. The clock theory is checked and rejected with evidence: dayNumber() counts whole UTC calendar days, and Mei Chen, 84 days on exactly, is already cleared.

It finds the second fault, which is a safety problem the user did not ask about: the mobile unit writes unpadded dates (`2026-7-20`), and `.sort()` orders them as text, so Gus Hale's 20 July mobile donation sorts after his 2 October one and he is cleared to give a month after donating. The fix orders by real date (normalising or using dayNumber), not by editing the history export.
Regression tests cover a deferral after a donation and a mix of padded and unpadded dates, and the existing 84-day tests still pass.

`npm run clinic -- 2026-11-03` is rerun and shows Priya (due from 2 November) and Tomas cleared, Gus not due until 25 December, and Mei, Sara, Olu and Ken unchanged. The reply flags Gus prominently as someone who was wrongly cleared, and its claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: The rink sheet in agent-suites/fixtures/bowls-club is turning captains down for no reason. `npm run sheet -- 2026-11-14` says Kestrels and Wrens can't have rinks 2 and 3 on the Saturday morning because they're taken, but nobody else asked for them. It started this season when rink 6 opened, so my guess is whoever added it numbered the rinks from 0 and everything's shifted along by one. Could you sort it out?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: allocate() in src/rinks.mjs builds `Array(RINKS).fill([])`, so all six rinks share one array and a booking on any rink makes every other rink look taken in that session. The fix gives each rink its own list (for example `Array.from({ length: RINKS }, () => [])`), not a dedupe or retry.
The numbering theory is checked and rejected with evidence: rinks are indexed with `rink - 1` throughout and rink 1 to 5 bookings land on the right rink once the arrays are separate.

It finds the second fault the first one hides, which the user half-suspected for the wrong reason: problemWith() refuses `request.rink >= RINKS`, so rink 6 itself is 'no such rink' (Owls in the morning, Harriers in the evening). The bound becomes `> RINKS` while 0 and 7 are still refused.
Regression tests cover bookings on two different rinks in one session and a booking on rink 6, and the existing tests pass.

`npm run sheet -- 2026-11-14` is rerun and shows Kestrels, Wrens and Owls on rinks 2, 3 and 6 in the morning, Harriers on 6 in the evening, and only Swifts (rink 1, genuinely taken by Harriers), Ravens (rink 4, taken by Kestrels) and Wrens' rink 7 turned down. The reply's claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: The summer reading leaderboard in agent-suites/fixtures/reading-challenge takes ages now that every branch library's logs are in. `npm run perf` says the median is about 650 ms. Can you get it under 15 ms? The board has to come out exactly the same, same order and all, because the certificates are printed from it. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 650 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 15 ms with errors at zero and the same work (896 children, 509 medals). Behaviour is identical: ISBNs matched without hyphens and spaces, the first catalogue entry winning for a repeated ISBN, names trimmed, a book counted at its first log within 18 July to 31 August inclusive, logs at the same minute kept in input order, children with no counted book left off, and the final tie-break still by `localeCompare` (not a plain `<` that puts `Ben` before `amy`). The caller's logs are not reordered.
Each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted rather than kept.

The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: leaderboard() filters every log for each child, and `books.find()` normalises the whole catalogue's ISBNs with a regular expression for every log, with `seen.includes()` and Date parsing on top. Indexing the catalogue once and grouping logs by child in one pass is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: The flood wardens run the alerts in agent-suites/fixtures/river-gauges every few minutes, and on a month of the whole catchment it's crawling: `npm run perf` reports a median of about 500 ms. Can you get it under 20 ms? The alert periods must come out exactly as they do now, because the wardens' rota is built from them. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 500 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 20 ms with errors at zero and the same work (99 periods, 7348 alert readings). Behaviour is identical: failed readings dropped before the window, a gap or a repeated timestamp breaking the four-reading window, a mean exactly at the threshold not alerting, a gauge without a threshold never alerting, and the period order by start then gauge. The mean is still summed over the four readings in order, so a running sum that adds and subtracts (and drifts in floating point, moving means that sit on the threshold) is not used, or is shown to give identical results.
Each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted rather than kept.

The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: alertPeriods() rebuilds each reading's window with `mine.filter()` over the gauge's whole month (quadratic), parses every timestamp into a Date again inside the window check and the sort comparator, and filters the whole feed once per gauge. Grouping by gauge once, parsing each time once and looking back three readings is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: At the end of a big store sale the office in agent-suites/fixtures/cattle-auction waits ages for the results and buyer totals. `npm run perf` puts it at about 700 ms on a full day. Can you get it under 15 ms? Invoices go out from these numbers, so the results and totals have to be exactly what they are now, to the penny. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 700 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 15 ms with errors at zero and the same work (346 lots sold, 250 buyers). Behaviour is identical: paddles matched ignoring case and spaces with the registered paddle reported, unregistered bidders ignored, bids on the hammer counted, a retraction covering every earlier bid by that bidder on that lot (with several retractions handled), equal amounts going to the earlier bid and then to the one listed first, unsold lots still reporting their highest bid, and the premium and totals computed exactly as before so no total moves by a fraction of a penny.
Each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted rather than kept.

The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: saleResults() filters every bid for each lot, and for every matching bid scans the bidder list and the retractions with paddles normalised and times parsed into Dates each time, then copies and sorts to find the top bid; buyerTotals() filters all results per bidder. Grouping bids by lot, indexing bidders and retractions once and finding the winner in one pass is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: The badge records in agent-suites/fixtures/scout-badges use cryptic field names. Please rename `bc`, `nm` and `lvl` to `code`, `name` and `stage` everywhere, data/awards.json included, so the next leader who picks this up can read it. Don't leave the old names around as aliases. `npm run census` goes straight into the district office's import, and the leaders use `npm run awards` and `npm run section` every week, so all three have to print exactly what they print now.

criteria: Every user is found, including the ones a search for `.bc`, `.nm` and `.lvl` misses: sortBy() is called with the field names as strings (`'lvl', 'nm'` in awardsFor() and `'lvl'` in bin/section.mjs), and data/sections.json names the field each section filters on (`"field": "lvl"`), which forSection() reads as `award[rule.field]`.

The outside name is kept: censusCsv() in src/census.mjs builds the heading row from `Object.keys()` and the rows from `Object.values()`, so renaming the fields would silently change the district office's import headings to `code,name,stage`. The census gets an explicit column mapping that keeps `bc,nm,lvl,scout,at` and the column order, and the reply says why those three names survive there.

data/awards.json and data/sections.json use the new names, the string stage (`"lvl": "1"`) is still read as a number, no aliases or dual reads of the old names are left, and the README and tests use the new names.
Output is shown to be identical by capturing `npm run census`, `npm run awards` for each scout and `npm run section` for each section before and after, and the tests pass.
The reply lists each migrated site, including the string keys, the section rules and the census headings, and how equivalence was checked.

claim.prompt: `quotePermit` in agent-suites/fixtures/fishing-permits takes five positional arguments and the counter staff keep getting the order wrong when they add things. Can you change it to take a single options object, `{ water, days, angler, rods, concession }`, and move everything in the project over to that? I don't want the positional form left lying around inside the project. Nothing anyone sees may change: `npm run quote`, `bulk`, `renewals` and `cheapest` have to print exactly what they print now, and the club website's booking page uses this package's public entry from its own repository, which we can't touch, so that has to keep working as it does today.

criteria: Every caller is found, including the ones a search for `quotePermit(` with positional arguments misses or misreads: `lakeDayTicket` in src/presets.mjs is `quotePermit.bind(null, 'lake', 1)`; bin/renewals.mjs spreads positional arrays stored in data/renewals.json (`quotePermit(...member.lastQuote)`), so either the data becomes objects or the code maps each array by position; bin/bulk.mjs reads the CSV columns in a different order (`angler,rods,water,days`) and passes undefined holes; the presets pass `undefined` for rods; and the tests call it positionally.

The outside contract is kept: src/index.mjs re-exports `quotePermit as quote`, which the booking page calls positionally, so the public `quote` (and `priceFor`, `seasonTicket`, `weekTicket`) keep their positional signatures, with `quote` becoming a small positional adapter at the boundary, while `quotePermit` itself has no positional or dual mode. The reply explains that decision.

Defaults behave as before for both missing and explicitly undefined options: destructuring defaults (or equivalent) keep `days` defaulting to the water's minimum and `concession` defaulting to `angler === 'junior'`; merging a defaults object with a spread (`{ ...DEFAULTS, ...options }`) is wrong because the migrated callers pass `undefined` values that would override the defaults.

Equivalence is shown by capturing every command's output (including the rejected and error cases and exit codes) before and after, and by comparing the old and new function across combinations of left-out and undefined options; the tests pass.
The reply lists each migrated site, including the bound preset, the spread renewal data and the public adapter, and how equivalence was checked.

claim.prompt: src/library.mjs in agent-suites/fixtures/mobile-library has grown into one big file with the time helpers, the stops, the timetable, the printing and the commands all mixed together. Please split it into separate modules by concern and point everything at the module that now owns each piece. I don't want library.mjs kept around as a re-export file. Watch out: the run sheet print formats are loaded on demand, and holds.mjs and library.mjs import each other; both of those have to keep working. The drivers and the enquiry desk use `npm run van` every day, so every command must print exactly what it prints now, errors included.

criteria: Every runtime-resolved user is found, not just the static imports: bin/van.mjs dynamically imports library.mjs and looks the command up by name on the module namespace (`library[`${name}Command`]`), so the dispatch must point at the module that exports the commands (and, if it becomes a plain object lookup, must not pick up inherited names); printRun's `import(`./formats/${format}.mjs`)` and holdsCommand's `import('./holds.mjs')` resolve relative to the file they are in; the format modules import helpers from '../library.mjs'; and `new URL('../data/stops.json', import.meta.url)` depends on where the stops code lands.

The circular imports are made safe rather than just moved: the top-level `ROUTES = groupByDay(STOPS)` and `STOPS = loadStops()` are evaluated at load time, so a split that leaves the stops and timetable modules importing each other (for example describeStop next to STOPS calling nextVisit) throws a TDZ ReferenceError for some entry points. The result keeps load-time data in a leaf module or otherwise breaks the cycle, and the holds cycle still loads whichever module is imported first.

The private helpers shared across concerns (parseDate, formatDate, dayName) are exported from one owner rather than duplicated; library.mjs is deleted with no re-export barrel; tests import from the new modules.

Equivalence is shown by capturing `npm run van` stdout, stderr and exit code before and after for every command, both formats, an unknown format, an unknown command and the error cases, and by loading each new module as an entry point; the tests pass.
The reply lists the new modules and what moved where, calls out the dynamic dispatch, the format paths and how the cycles were handled, and says how equivalence was checked.

claim.prompt: The league secretary wants every bowler's scores and average for the handicap sheet, so agent-suites/fixtures/tenpin-league needs to score games. Add `scoreGame(sheet)` in src/score.mjs that returns the total for a sheet like the ones in data/games.json. A sheet is ten frames separated by single spaces. A frame is `X` for a strike, a first ball followed by `/` for a spare, or two balls that knock down nine pins or fewer between them, where a ball is a digit 1 to 9 or `-` for none. In the tenth frame a strike earns two more balls and a spare one more, written in the same frame (`XX7`, `8/X`, `X9-`). Scoring is the usual: a strike counts ten plus the next two balls, a spare ten plus the next one. `x` works as well as `X`. A sheet that breaks these rules throws a RangeError quoting the sheet, and anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError. Then add `--bowler <name>` to `npm run games`: list that bowler's games in the order bowled, each line followed by two spaces and the score, then `Average: <n>`, their average rounded down to a whole pin. The name should match whatever the case, ignoring spaces around it. A game whose sheet can't be read stays in the list with `?` for its score, is left out of the average and is named on stderr, and the command still exits 0. A missing name, or one with no games, exits 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `games: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: strikes and spares carrying their bonus balls, gutter balls and `-/`, every tenth-frame shape (XXX, XX9, X9/, X9-, X-/, 9/X, an open tenth) and the broken ones (a tenth strike or spare missing its bonus balls, bonus balls after an open tenth, X5X, XX/, too many balls), nine or eleven frames, a normal frame adding up to ten without `/`, `X/` or `-X`, lower case, the empty string, numeric strings such as `300`, non-string values, and the CLI's rounded-down averages (Ann's 184.5 shown as 184), the `?` rows for Ben's and Dev's unreadable sheets, case and space matching of names, and the exit-2 cases with nothing on stdout.

The implementation is small (one pass that turns frames into balls, then one scoring loop, for example) and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example `0` as a ball, doubled or trailing spaces, an empty or whitespace-only name, what the average line says when none of a bowler's games can be read, and the exact wording of the stderr lines).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --bowler and the sheet rules, and the scoring rules live in one place.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and sample output for a bowler with an unreadable game.

claim.prompt: Over Christmas the dairy shuts and the float has to carry the extra milk the day before, so agent-suites/fixtures/milk-round should work out each day's load. Add `dropsOn(date, customers, closed)` in src/drops.mjs that returns what goes out on a date as `[{ name, pints }]`, in round order, leaving out anyone who gets nothing. `customers` and `closed` are shaped like data/customers.json and data/closed.json. A customer gets their pints on each of their days, but not on a day inside one of their `away` spells (first and last day included; `away` can be missing). Nothing goes out on a closed day. A drop that falls on a closed day goes out instead on the nearest earlier day the dairy is open, on top of whatever is due then, so the Thursday before a Friday and Saturday shutdown carries all three days. If the customer is away on the day the drop was due, or on the day it would move to, there's nothing to carry. The date has to be a real date written exactly as YYYY-MM-DD, or it throws a RangeError quoting it, and anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError. It has to give the same answer whatever timezone the computer is set to. Then add `--drops <date>` to `npm run customers` to print one line per drop like `2  Mrs Okafor, 4 Mill Lane`, then `Total pints: <n>`, or `No deliveries on <date>.` if nothing goes out. A missing or bad date exits 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `milk: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: ordinary days, a closed day itself, a Friday and Saturday both carried to Thursday, a Saturday-only customer carried past Friday, New Year's Day carried to the 31st, away spells including their first and last days, away on the closed day (only that drop is lost) versus away on the day it moves to (Ivy Marsh and Joe Brennan get nothing on the 24th), a missing `away`, invalid dates (30 February, 29 February outside a leap year, month 13, single-digit parts, slashes, a time part, surrounding spaces), non-string values including a Date, a day across a clock change, and the CLI's Christmas Eve load of 9 pints, the no-deliveries line and the exit-2 cases.

The implementation is small, does its date arithmetic one timezone-safe way (UTC day numbers or plain calendar dates), and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example what happens when every earlier day is closed or the date is before the round starts, whether a closed date passed in an odd format counts, an away spell whose end is before its start, duplicated weekdays, and the exact stderr wording).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --drops and the carrying rule, and the date and closing rules live in one place.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and the Christmas Eve output.

claim.prompt: The churchwarden puts the numbers up on the hymn board before each service and keeps getting the verse lists wrong, so agent-suites/fixtures/hymn-boards should read them. Add `parseHymn(text, book)` in src/hymns.mjs, where `book` is shaped like data/hymns.json, returning `{ number, title, verses }` with `verses` as the list of verse numbers to sing. A hymn is written as its number, with no leading zeros, and it has to be in the book. It can be followed by a space, a `v` (either case), an optional space and a verse list, like `372 v1-3,5` or `640 V 1, 4`. The list is single verses and ranges such as `6-8`, separated by commas with an optional space after each comma. A range runs from a lower verse to a higher one, the verses have to go up with no repeats or overlaps, and each one must be between 1 and the hymn's verse count. With no list, it's all the verses. Anything else throws a RangeError quoting the text, and anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError. Then add `--board <date>` to `npm run services` to print that day's board: one line per hymn with the number, two spaces, the title, two spaces, then `all` if every verse is sung or otherwise the verses like `1, 2, 3, 5`, and finally `Verses to sing: <n>`. If any hymn that day can't be read, print nothing on stdout, name each bad one on stderr and exit 1. A missing or invalid date, or a date with no service, exits 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `hymns: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: a bare number giving every verse, single verses and ranges in either case of `v` with and without the optional spaces, the last verse and one past it, a range written high to low, repeats, out-of-order and overlapping verses, an empty list and stray commas or dashes, numbers missing from the book, leading zeros, and numeric look-alikes such as `1e2`, `0x64`, `100.0` and `+8` (which `Number()` would accept), surrounding spaces, non-string values, and the CLI's `all` for an explicit full range (`372 v1-6`, `475 V1-4`), verse totals, Trinity 23's two bad hymns both named with exit 1, and the exit-2 date cases.

The implementation is small (one pattern for the hymn and one for each list item, for example) and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example a one-verse range such as `2-2`, spaces around a dash, no space before the `v`, a book with duplicate numbers, a hymn listed twice in a service, and the exact stderr wording).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --board and the verse notation, and the notation rules live in one place.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and a sample board.

claim.prompt:
A few things from the school office for agent-suites/fixtures/school-dinners. One commit each on this branch, please.

1. Maya Patel's mum says she's been billed £44.20 for the half term, but Maya was off with chickenpox on the 14th and 15th and that's in the register. Please fix it, and add a test so it doesn't creep back.
2. Add `--allergies` to `npm run kitchen` so the sheet also lists who needs an allergy plate that day, with their class and what they can't have.
3. Orders now close at 9:15 rather than 9:30. Please change it on the kitchen sheet and in the README.
4. Mrs Okoye in the kitchen also needs to know how many packed lunches to expect so she can set out the hall.

criteria: Each item is done at its cause: isAbsent() in src/register.mjs only matches an absence's single `date`, so `from`/`to` absences are ignored; handling ranges with both days included fixes Maya (15 dinners, £39.00) and also Leo Grant (14 dinners, £36.40) and Dan Evans (15 dinners, still free), which the office did not mention, and the kitchen count for the 14th drops from 6 to 5 because the kitchen uses the same register. The allergy list covers only pupils who are in that day and having a school dinner (not Chloe on the 7th, not Maya on the 14th, and Noah's packed lunch needs no plate, or that choice is stated). ORDERS_CLOSE and the README both say 9:15.
Item 4 is recognised as already done (the kitchen sheet already prints `Packed lunches`) and reported as such, with no empty or cosmetic commit made for it.

There are three commits for the three real changes, each verified; the absence commit carries a regression test that fails on the old code (ideally covering both ends of a range), and edge cases are named, such as a one-day range, a range running past the half term, or an unknown date with --allergies.
Nothing outside the items changes (the register data is not rewritten into single dates to dodge the fix), and main is untouched.
The reply summarises each item with its commit and how it was checked, says plainly that item 4 needed no change, and mentions Leo's bill, Dan's count and the kitchen numbers changing too.

claim.prompt:
Some odds and ends for agent-suites/fixtures/window-cleaning from me and Kev. One commit per thing on this branch, please.

criteria: Each item is done at its cause: round() in src/round.mjs keeps `due > monday`, so anyone due on the Monday is dropped; including the Monday puts Mr Dawson and also Mrs Kaur (10 Elm Road, eight-weekly, also due 2 November) on the round, and Mr Price and Mrs Hall on the week of 9 November, which nobody mentioned. owed() matches payments to customers exactly, and cash taken on the phone was entered as `c03` and `c07`; matching ids case-insensitively clears Ms Osei and also Mr Lowe's £12, bringing the total owed from £80.00 to £53.00, without rewriting the payment records.

--by-street sorts by street and then by house number as a number (3, 10, 14 Elm Road; 1, 5, 21 Station Road), and Flat 3, 22 Mill Lane is treated as number 22 on Mill Lane, after 12 Mill Lane. The new number replaces 07700 900118 in the code, the README and docs/leaflet.md.
Item 5 is recognised as already done (the round already prints each customer's price) and reported as such, with no empty or cosmetic commit made for it.

There are four commits for the four real changes, each verified; the cash commit carries a regression test that fails on the old code, and edge cases are named, such as a customer due on the Sunday, an address the street sort can't parse, or a payment for a customer id that doesn't exist.

Nothing outside the items changes, and main is untouched. The reply summarises each item with its commit and how it was checked, says plainly that item 5 needed no change, and mentions Mrs Kaur and Mr Lowe changing too.

claim.prompt:
Show committee list for agent-suites/fixtures/county-show. Straight onto main is fine, one commit per item.

1. In class 7 Gwen Pryce's runner beans got 18 points and the results put her third, behind a 9 and an 8.
2. Tom Pryce is 15 and `npm run fees` says he owes £1.00. The schedule says 15 and under enter free. Please fix it and add a test.
3. The treasurer wants `npm run fees -- --unpaid` to show only the people who still owe us.
4. The show has moved to Bracken Fields this year, but the README and the heading on `npm run results` still say Ashby Rec.
5. The trophy table needs to know which village each winner is from, so please put that on the results.

criteria: Each item is done at its cause: the points from data/points.csv stay strings and placings() compares them as text, so a single-digit score beats a double-digit one; comparing them as numbers fixes Gwen in class 7 and also class 3 (Gwen 1st, Sita Rao 2nd, Harold Venn 3rd) and class 15 (Tom 1st, Lily 2nd), which the committee did not mention, while class 12 stays as it was, and the prize money moves to Gwen £6, Sita £5, Tom £5, Harold £3, Lily £2, Owen £2. fees() uses `age < 15`, so 15 itself is charged; `<= 15` frees Tom.

--unpaid lists only exhibitors with a fee still owed, so juniors who enter free and people who have paid are left out. The venue change replaces Ashby Rec only, keeping the show's name, Ashby & District Show, and Ashby as a village.
Item 5 is recognised as already done (the results already print each winner's village) and reported as such, with no empty or cosmetic commit made for it.

The fix sets the dark tokens on the root element when `data-theme='dark'`, including `--muted` and `color-scheme`, and limits the system dark block to when Light is not chosen (for example `:root:not([data-theme='light'])`). Each mode then looks exactly as the system modes did before, and theme.js, the markup and the token values are unchanged, with no !important. Sharing one dark token list between the two paths rather than keeping two copies is better.
The result is checked by rendering or by resolving the cascade in all six combinations: system light and dark, with the switch on System, Light and Dark.

The reply lists the causes, the changes and how they were checked, and mentions what remains: the duplicated dark token lists can drift apart if both are kept, and a saved choice may flash the system theme before the deferred theme.js runs, which is not silently changed.
